chain: 2 hops: local Debian 13 client VM (home internet via a consumer VPN) -> AWS relay avpn-relay (eu-north-1, t3.micro, NitroTPM 2.0) -> OCI exit (me-dubai-1, Ubuntu 22.04)

built_with.relay: avpn cloud aws relay --apply (tagged; IMDSv2 required, standard credits, encrypted gp3, UDP 41194 and SSH from one address only)
built_with.relay_host: avpn cloud host setup (TSS2 libraries, journal in RAM, package installed, keys sealed host+tpm2)
built_with.exit_firewall: avpn cloud oci allow --apply (UDP 4444 from the relay only; other rules unchanged) plus a runtime host accept for the relay only
built_with.operator: Nitrokey FIDO2 Ed25519 assertion + sealed ML-DSA-65 (one PIN + touch)

protection.relay: systemd-creds host+tpm2 (keys generated on the relay)
protection.exit: none: Ubuntu 22.04 systemd 249 predates systemd-creds; keys generated on the exit, root-only files

relay.finding: the persistent system journal held sshd records of the admin's address (the user's own address)
relay.fix: journal in RAM only (Storage=volatile), now part of avpn cloud host setup

exit.note: sudo logs the admin's own command lines on this shared host; system logging there was left unchanged

published_redactions: Public addresses, host names and key fingerprints were replaced with documentation values (RFC 5737) before publication; the measurements are unchanged.
